Dot Picture Rules

Numbered dots are spread over the board. Join them in order, and a picture appears.

The rules

Joining dots
Tap dot 1, then dot 2, then 3 and so on. A line joins each dot to the one before; joined dots turn black. The number you are looking for is printed in bold.
A wrong dot
A tap on another dot changes nothing. A short note says which dot you tapped and which one comes next.
The goal
After the last dot the line closes back to dot 1. The dots go away, the finished picture appears with a few extra lines, and its name is shown.
Levels
Easy (for children): 10 to 15 big dots far apart. Medium: about 25 dots. Hard: about 40 dots. Very hard (for adults): about 50 to 60 dots close together; the picture only shows at the end. Each level has five pictures, one after the other.
Magnified view
The board always shows the whole picture at one fixed size; a tap only adds the dot and the line, nothing moves. From medium on the dots lie close together and the numbers are smaller. A tap counts for the dot you look for when it is one of the two dots nearest to your finger. "Magnify" shows a fixed part around the next dot with the dots further apart; "Go to the next dot" moves that part, "Whole picture" goes back.
Undo and hint
Undo takes back the last dot. The hint gives the next dot a double ring.
